stem:
The diagram shows a concave mirror used in two ways: held close to a small object for enlarged viewing, and facing parallel light rays that meet at a point for light concentration.

Which claim correctly matches concave tools to those needs?

options.text: A concave mirror can give an enlarged image of a nearby object and can also concentrate parallel light rays toward a focus.
Only a plane mirror can enlarge a nearby object; a concave mirror never enlarges.
A convex mirror concentrates parallel rays to a focus and enlarges nearby objects.
A concave mirror enlarges only when the object is far from the mirror, never when it is close.

teacher.key_rationale: A concave mirror (or lens) can enlarge a close object for viewing and can concentrate parallel light at a focus. Swapping in plane or convex roles, or requiring the object to be far for enlargement, miss those concave uses.
teacher.figure_note: Two panels: concave mirror with nearby object and enlarged image; concave mirror focusing parallel rays to a point.
